seo.title: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Wokingham | Fit-Only Installation | Install My Bathroom
seo.description: The sanitaryware, brassware and tile brands we fit for Wokingham clients, and how our fit-only installation model works alongside your own supplier choices.

h1: Bathroom Brands We Fit in Wokingham

hero.intro: We don't sell bathrooms in Wokingham — we fit them. That's the fit-only model in a sentence: you choose and buy your own sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture, from whichever showroom or retailer you prefer, and we install it to the standard the brand and your room both deserve. Over 30 years of fitting high-end bathrooms, certain brands turn up on our Wokingham specification sheets more often than others — some suited to the period detail of the Georgian and Victorian townhouses and villas around the market place, others just as at home in the inter-war, post-war and new-build estate housing that makes up much of the rest of the town — each with its own installation detail that matters more than most people expect before the first fixing goes into the wall.

sections.heading: The fit-only model explained
sections.body: Nothing about the fit-only model changes which brands you can bring to a Wokingham installation — if anything, it widens the choice, because we're not trying to steer you toward stock we hold or a supplier we have an arrangement with. You buy from the showroom or retailer you trust, at the price you've agreed, and we check it all at survey: waste sizes, tap centres, fixing requirements and whether everything you've chosen is actually compatible with everything else, before strip-out starts rather than after a delivery is already sitting in the hallway.

sections.heading: Sanitaryware and shower toilets we fit
sections.body: Geberit's concealed cisterns, wall-hung WCs and AquaClean shower toilets are the sanitaryware brand we fit most often in Wokingham, and correct frame selection matters more here than with most brands, because the cistern and pan weight sits entirely on the carrier frame rather than the wall tiles — worth getting right in an older, solid-masonry townhouse near the market place as much as a modern estate home. We also fit a good deal of Laufen, the Swiss manufacturer whose SaphirKeramik material lets it produce basins and pans with noticeably finer rims and sharper geometry than standard vitreous china allows; that thinness is the main thing we plan around, since the pieces are less forgiving of a knock in transit or on site than a heavier, conventional basin. Where Duravit is specified, it's usually alongside SensoWash shower toilet seats or a full ME by Starck suite, and the detail worth settling early is whether the installation route is Duravit's own DuraSystem frame or a standard concealed cistern frame — the two aren't interchangeable once a wall is boarded. On projects that mix a cast-iron bath with wall-hung sanitaryware, Kohler's range spans both disciplines at once, which means planning for heavy-item logistics and standard structural fixing side by side rather than treating the project as a single generic approach.

sections.heading: Brassware and showers we fit
sections.body: GROHE covers a wide span of the work we do in Wokingham — thermostatic shower valves and mixer taps on mid-range refits, Rapid SL cistern frames behind wall-hung WCs, and digital shower and smart water products on more specified projects. The range is broad enough that the installation detail changes considerably depending on which part of it you've chosen, which is why we work through exactly what's been specified at survey rather than treating 'GROHE' as a single fitting job. On the more design-led projects, Dornbracht sits at the top end of what we fit — a German brassware house known for sculptural handle and spout design and for finishes that are genuinely difficult to replicate elsewhere — and the margin for error is smaller: a scuff on a brushed finish or a rough-in set a few millimetres wrong is far more visible, and far more expensive to put right, than the same mistake on a mainstream brand. Crosswater's contemporary brassware and shower systems run heavily on concealed valves, digital controls and minimal deck-mounted taps designed to disappear into the wall or worktop, which means the work that determines how well a Crosswater shower performs happens largely before the tiler arrives — wall build-up, pipework depth, and the water pressure and flow the valve actually needs.

sections.heading: Baths, trays and tiling we fit
sections.body: Bette manufactures baths and shower trays from titanium-steel finished with fused glass enamel — a material that's harder and more scratch-resistant than acrylic, but unforgiving of a poorly built base underneath it, so we fit Bette baths and trays with the substructure, levelling and acoustic isolation the material actually needs, rather than treating it like any other bath. Where a Wokingham client wants brassware and sanitaryware that suit a Georgian or Victorian townhouse rather than a contemporary estate home, Burlington turns up often — pedestal and wall-hung basins, close-coupled and high-level WCs, roll-top baths and period-style brassware reproduced with a modern fixing standard underneath the traditional silhouette, where getting the period look right depends on fixing choices that aren't visible once the room is finished. Matki's largely frameless shower enclosures leave very little trim to hide an inaccurate opening, so measuring, wall fixing and sequencing against tiling and the tray get planned in that order, not worked out on the day. And Porcelanosa's large-format porcelain is dense, rectified and dimensionally precise, which punishes an uneven substrate or an inconsistent joint far more visibly than a smaller tile would — the floor or wall gets checked and prepared flat first, then set with the correct bed coverage, joint width and lippage control.

sections.heading: Choosing brands for Wokingham's period and newer homes
sections.body: Wokingham's historic core holds a good number of Georgian and Victorian townhouses and villas, many later divided or extended as the town grew, while the wider town has expanded substantially through inter-war, post-war and contemporary estate development. That mix doesn't dictate which brands suit which property — a Geberit frame or a Matki frameless screen fits into a Victorian townhouse as readily as a newer estate home once the wall or floor underneath has been properly checked — but it does change what gets checked first. A heavy Bette steel bath or a cast-iron Kohler tub needs a suspended timber floor confirmed for deflection before it goes anywhere near the room, which is exactly what the survey is for, whichever brand ends up being specified.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy my bathroom from you?
faqs.a: No. We're fit-only — you buy your sanitaryware, brassware, tiles and furniture from whichever showroom or retailer you choose, and we install it.

faqs.q: Can you fit a bathroom with products from several different brands mixed together?
faqs.a: Yes, this is the norm. We check waste sizes, tap centres and fixing requirements across every brand involved at survey, so everything is confirmed compatible before strip-out starts.

faqs.q: Do you have a preferred brand you push clients toward?
faqs.a: No. The fit-only model means we don't hold stock or have a sales arrangement with any particular manufacturer — the brands mentioned here are simply the ones that appear most often on the specifications our Wokingham clients bring to us.

faqs.q: Can traditional brassware like Burlington suit a Georgian or Victorian Wokingham townhouse?
faqs.a: Yes, and it's a common choice for the town's period properties near the market place. The range reproduces classic pedestal basins, close-coupled WCs and period-style brassware on a modern fixing standard, which we set out so the pipe runs and fixings sit correctly behind the traditional profile.

faqs.q: Does a heavy bath or cast-iron tub need anything extra checking in an older Wokingham property?
faqs.a: Often, yes. A Bette steel bath or a Kohler cast-iron tub has real weight and needs accurate, even bearing underneath it — on a ground floor with suspended timber construction, we confirm that structural support at survey before the bath is ordered.

faqs.q: Will you fit products bought from an online retailer rather than a showroom?
faqs.a: Yes, provided the specification is confirmed compatible at survey. We check this regardless of where a product was bought from.

image.heroPrompt: Purpose: hero image for the Wokingham brands page, a close/mid detail shot implying a choice between traditional and contemporary brand character rather than a full room. Subject and action: a traditional cross-head pedestal basin tap mounted beside a sleek contemporary concealed shower control panel set into dark stone tiling, the two styles placed close together as if mid-way through a specification decision, no running water. Setting and work-stage: a finished bathroom wall inside a renovated Wokingham townhouse blending period and estate-home fittings, late afternoon, soft overcast daylight entering from an unseen window to the side. Composition: close-to-fixture mid shot centred where the traditional tap meets the contemporary control panel, dark basalt stone tiling filling the lower third of the frame, wall tiling soft and slightly out of focus behind. Light and materials: dark basalt stone tiling with natural flecking, brushed bronze traditional cross-head tap alongside a brushed bronze contemporary shower control panel, soft overcast daylight falling evenly from one side only, creating gentle but uneven shadow rather than flat light. Constraints: no people, no text, no logos, no brand names visible on any fixture; no LED lighting strips anywhere in frame; no symmetrical twin-basin staging; no uniform gold or amber colour wash; no hanging plants, florals or candles; no water shown running; fixtures should show faint, believable handling marks rather than uniform showroom-new gloss.
image.heroAlt: Close-up of a traditional brushed bronze cross-head basin tap beside a contemporary concealed shower control panel on dark basalt stone tiling in a Wokingham bathroom
